title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Preregistered, Artifact-Backed Evaluation of Input-Sanitization and Deterministic Verification Against Adversarial Intents
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured whether template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (and at-most-one automated repair) changes the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated device CLI configurations under adversarially mutated intents. The frozen run used the declared generator gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 within an orchestration adapter. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; complete paired outcomes used in the primary analysis = 141. Observed per-pair acceptance: Baseline 135/141 (95.7447%); Guarded 141/141 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.04255319148936165; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. We reconcile preregistration wording vs the formal estimand, describe shared_initial_candidate pipeline semantics, disclose a protocol deviation (unset runtime sampling temperature), and discuss operational interpretation and limitations. All principal numeric claims are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts (execution manifest cited as [14]).

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are increasingly proposed to translate high-level operator intent into device CLI to accelerate NetOps. However, generated outputs can violate sequencing constraints, CLI grammar, or safety invariants; adversarially crafted inputs may exacerbate such failures. Prior prototypes show that coupling LLM generation with deterministic verification and localized repair improves observable outcomes, but evaluations often measure token- or reference-match rather than validator-centered deployability. We therefore ask a narrowly scoped, preregistered question amenable to confirmatory inference: how effective are template-based input sanitization and deterministic verifier-gating (with at-most-one automated repair) at changing the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations when inputs are adversarially mutated? The preregistered formal estimand measures the paired difference in validator acceptance (guarded − baseline) using shared_initial_candidate semantics so that downstream guarded-pipeline elements are the causal factors under test. Contributions: (1) a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment executed end-to-end; (2) an explicit, artifact-grounded description of per-condition pipeline semantics with shared_initial_candidate reuse; (3) quantitative confirmatory results showing a small but statistically detectable absolute change in validator acceptance on a synthetic adversarial-intent bank; (4) reconciliation of preregistration language with the formal estimand and disclosure of a protocol deviation with reproducibility guidance.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network verification tools (Header Space Analysis, NetPlumber, VeriFlow) provide semantics-focused checks (reachability, isolation, ordering) suitable as deployment gates for generated configurations [1–3]. Empirical NetOps/LLM studies (e.g., NetConfEval, NetLLMBench) and surveys report that model-only generation produces syntax and higher-level semantic errors and emphasize fragmented evaluation practices that lack validator-centered deployability metrics [4–7]. Generate–validate–repair architectures—where an LLM produces a draft, a verifier checks it, and bounded repairs are attempted—have been shown in prototypes to improve verified outcomes given precise verifier diagnostics [8,3]. Security work documents prompt-injection and indirect prompt attacks that motivate input-sanitization and gating defenses in LLM-integrated pipelines [9]. These prior findings motivate our preregistered, validator-centered estimand and shared_initial_candidate design.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study cand-2026-03 preregistered a single primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. For each adversarial intent the binary outcome equals 1 if the deterministic validator would accept the final candidate for deployment and 0 otherwise. The confirmatory test is an exact two-sided McNemar on paired outcomes; bootstrap percentile 95% CIs use 10,000 resamples with seed = 1729. The preregistration, execution manifest, and analysis artifacts are archived and cited as a single repository artifact [14].

Design and task bank. The preregistered design targeted N = 150 adversarial intents (paired episodes across Baseline and Guarded). The synthetic intent templates exercise admin/MTU/VLAN updates, explicit required-sequence constraints (e.g., shutdown–change–restore), protected-interface rules, and mutation heuristics (string-level, token-insertion, slot-override). Scope is limited to these synthetic templates and the deterministic CLI semantics encoded in the validator; no production data were used.

Model, validator, and orchestration. The declared generator is gpt-5-mini and the validator is deterministic_netops_validator_v5; orchestration used a hosted generate–validate–repair adapter implementing the guarded pipeline. The guarded branch applies template-based sanitization prior to gating and allows at most one automated repair LLM call when policy permits. The execution manifest records the full run-level archive and provider-call accounting and is the primary machine-verifiable reference for execution and analysis [14].

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and missingness. Because generation semantics were registered as shared_initial_candidate, each pair used a single initial LLM draft: Baseline applied the validator to the shared draft; Guarded applied sanitizer ± permitted repair (at most one additional LLM call) and then the validator re-evaluated the final candidate. The preregistered missingness rule excluded paired units only when both paired runs were technical failures. The archived reconciliation reports completed_episodes = 282, failed_episodes = 18, and complete_pairs_included = 141; provider-call accounting and stage counts are archived [14].

Analysis plan. The primary analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1 (exact McNemar) with bootstrap percentile CIs (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Sensitivity analyses for technical failures were specified in the preregistration; secondary estimands (benign-control false-positive blocking) were preregistered but not executed in this run (see Results). All analysis parameters and outputs are archived [14].
sections.results:
Execution and raw counts. The run completed 282/300 planned episodes; applying the preregistered exclusion rule produced 141 complete pairs for primary analysis. Provider-call accounting in the archived reconciliation shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 156 total model-call events, 147 completed, and 9 failed; stage counts report 150 shared_initial_generation events and 6 repair-stage events [14].

Condition-level outcomes. Baseline accepted final candidates in 135/141 complete pairs (baseline success rate = 0.9574468085106383). Guarded accepted final candidates in 141/141 pairs (guarded success rate = 1.0).

Paired contingency and inference. The paired contingency table is n11 = 135, n10 = 6, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar test yields p = 0.03125. Observed paired point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165. The 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) is [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. All numeric outputs and test parameters are archived and reproducible from the analysis artifacts [14].

Discordant-case diagnostics and repairs. The six discordant (n10) pairs are associated with guarded-branch repair-stage activity (repair-stage count = 6 in the reconciliation artifacts). For each discordant pair the shared_initial_candidate was identical across conditions; the guarded pipeline used sanitizer normalization and/or a single permitted repair to convert a draft the validator would reject into a validator-accepted final candidate. Detailed per-episode validator traces and repair traces are archived for inspection [14].

Sensitivity to technical failures. Nine paired units were excluded because both paired runs failed technically. As a conservative, nonpreregistered sensitivity check treating excluded pairs as failures, baseline acceptance = 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded acceptance = 141/150 = 0.9400; this illustrates that technical failures reduced effective sample size but do not invert the observed paired difference under this conservative assumption. The missingness accounting is archived [14].

Unexecuted preregistered items. The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed in this run; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking rates are reported here (this omission is noted in the preregistration and archived manifest [14]).
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and bounds. The formal estimand measured validator acceptance-for-deployment; the observed small absolute increase (≈4.255 percentage points) reflects that sanitizer and bounded repair recovered reparable drafts that the baseline validator rejected. This outcome does not, by itself, demonstrate reduced attacker success under an attacker-centric definition: repairs could either restore intended semantics or unintentionally mask adversarial manipulation. Thus, conflating validator acceptance with attacker-centric safety is not warranted without an independent semantic-safety oracle.

Operational implications. In synthetic settings, sanitizer plus bounded automated repair can reduce operator rework by converting invalid drafts into validator-accepted candidates; this benefit depends on validator expressiveness and repair policy scope. Co-design of gating policies, repair bounds, and verifier coverage is required to avoid accepted-but-unsafe repairs in deployment.

Threats to validity. Internal: 18 technical failures reduced effective sample and triggered preregistered exclusions. Construct: the deterministic validator encodes CLI grammar, ordering, and protected-interface invariants but omits some protocol-level runtime semantics; acceptance is a partial proxy for safety. External: single generator (gpt-5-mini), single validator, and synthetic templates constrain generalizability. Conclusion: small absolute effect against a high baseline implies statistical detectability does not equate to broad operational impact.

Reproducibility note and protocol deviation. The archived model configuration recorded an unset runtime sampling temperature; this is disclosed as a protocol deviation because provider-side defaults can affect sampling determinism. To preserve paired comparability the pipeline used shared_initial_candidate semantics; provider-call accounting in the reconciliation artifact confirms the actual call pattern. For deterministic reproduction we recommend explicitly setting temperature = 0 when re-executing the archived manifest. The preregistration, execution manifest, and analysis artifacts are archived and cited as [14].

Recommendations. Execute the preregistered benign-control to measure false-positive blocking; preregister an attacker-centric estimand coupling validator acceptance with an independent semantic-safety oracle; diversify generators and validators across vendors and CLI dialects; and set explicit sampling parameters (e.g., temperature = 0) for deterministic reproduction. Each recommendation follows directly from the archived run-level artifacts and provider-call accounting [14].
sections.conclusion: A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment on a synthetic adversarial intent bank found that template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating and at-most-one automated repair produced a small but statistically detectable absolute increase in deterministic-validator-accepted LLM-generated configurations under the archived formal estimand (paired difference = 0.04255319148936165; p = 0.03125; 95% CI [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]). Diagnostics link the six discordant pairs to permitted repair calls that enabled acceptance. This formal-estimand improvement does not substitute for an attacker-centric safety measurement. The run is limited by synthetic scope, single-model/validator evaluation, and a protocol deviation (unset runtime temperature). Future work should execute the preregistered benign-control, measure attacker-centric estimands with an independent semantic-safety oracle, diversify models/validators, and fix sampling settings for reproducible deterministic runs. All principal numbers and reconciliation claims above are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts; the execution manifest is the primary archive cited here [14].

limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated.
A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; results are reported and interpreted with respect to the archived formal estimand.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
